# RustyNES v2.7.2 — "Bankroll"

The third release of the audit line that [ADR 0041](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-hardware-release-is-v3.0.0.md) put between v2.6.23 and the SuperStation One core (**v3.0.0**). It works from the core audit's mapper findings in [`docs/audits/`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/README.md), and its subject is cartridge memory: **every bank a cartridge has, and nothing it has not.**

Every behaviour here was written from the vendored nesdev wiki and pinned by a test that fails on the previous release first. **AccuracyCoin 144/144** (RAM decoder, 0 fail, 0 not run) and **nestest** were re-measured on the release tree, because this release changes what the CPU reads at `$6000-$7FFF`. The full `--features test-roms` workspace suite passes **2,659 tests, 0 failed** (v2.7.1: 2,629).

**The MiSTer sibling does not change in this release, and no new bitstream is cut.** No hardware has run any bitstream; the board session is v2.9.2.

## MMC1 reaches its upper 256 KiB

MMC1's PRG register addresses 256 KiB. SUROM and SXROM reach 512 KiB by reusing a CHR line: on boards with at most 8 KiB of CHR, the CHR bank register's bit 4 selects the 256 KiB half for the whole PRG window, the "fixed" bank included, and bits 3-2 select the 8 KiB PRG-RAM bank on SOROM (16 KiB) and SXROM (32 KiB). The code read four PRG bits and no RAM bank. It also treated SUROM's PRG line as SNROM's RAM-disable bit, so switching to the upper half switched the RAM off.

The oracle is holy_mapperel, whose SxROM driver tests exactly this. Its binary release ships no 512 KiB image, so two were built from the release's own source tag. That build reproduces all 17 committed release ROMs byte-for-byte, which is the evidence the new images come from the same program.

| ROM | v2.7.1 | v2.7.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `M1_P512K_CR8K_S8K` (SUROM) | `S*ROM`, `PRG RAM MISSING`, `0300` | `SUROM`, `512K PRG ROM`, `8K PRG RAM OK`, `0000` |
| `M1_P512K_CR8K_S32K` (SXROM) | `S*ROM`, `PRG RAM MISSING`, `0300` | `SXROM`, `512K PRG ROM`, `32K PRG RAM OK`, `0000` |

Both screens were rendered and read. Both ROMs join the pinned holy_mapperel net, whose other 17 snapshots are unchanged.

The same change also covers 4 KiB CHR mode, where the PPU's A12 decides which CHR register drives these lines as it renders. The wiki warns about exactly this. One committed ROM relies on it: Bregalad's "MMC1 WRAM disable scanline counter test" (`tests/roms/mmc1_a12`). Its grey raster bar now appears, where v2.7.1 drew none. Its snapshot was re-blessed, and reverting only the A12 selection brings back the old hash exactly. That ROM had been catalogued as an inert smoke test credited to tepples; its README now says what it tests and who wrote it.

## MMC5 banks its PRG-RAM, over the 64 KiB superset

`$5113` was stored and never read, and the RAM-mode pages of `$5114-$5116` were ignored, so every access landed in the first 8 KiB. Koei's large-RAM games use the other pages, and *Uncharted Waters* reads RAM back through a different CPU address than it wrote.

The first version implemented the wiki's per-board table: bit 2 as a chip select, and open bus where the declared size has no chip. The commercial-ROM comparison below caught what that costs. *L'Empereur* is an ETROM board (8 KiB battery chip plus 8 KiB work chip, per the wiki's board table), but its NES 2.0 header declares only the battery chip. Under the exact table its work RAM floated and the game stopped at its logo. The wiki anticipates exactly this: headers are unreliable here, and "emulating the PRG-RAM as 64K at all times can be used as a compatible superset for all games". That is what v2.7.2 does. The save file stays the header's battery-backed part, so save files keep their size, and a 16 KiB board saves only its first 8 KiB, as the wiki says.

## Namco 163 nametables and CIRAM-as-CHR

`$C000-$DFFF` now select each nametable quadrant: a value below `$E0` is a read-only 1 KiB CHR-ROM page, and `$E0` and up is console RAM (page A or B). CHR values `$E0-$FF` map console RAM as CHR-RAM unless `$E800` bit 6 or 7 disables it for that pattern half; those bits used to be masked off. The registers power on as the header's layout, so a game that never writes them renders exactly as before.

## `$6000-$7FFF` floats where nothing is there

The CPU bus holds the last value driven onto it, and a cartridge read that nothing answers returns that value. The mapper trait assumed all of `$6000-$FFFF` was mapped, so a board with no RAM there read a made-up `$00`. The audit named four such boards. A sweep over every NES 2.0 mapper number found **205** board variants.

The fix is at the trait default: `$6000-$7FFF` floats exactly when the board has no save RAM. That is sound because v2.7.1 made every save-RAM board expose it. The same test checks the converse: a board reported unmapped must not actually drive data there. That check found seven boards with ROM or registers in the window, and they stay mapped.

Two more things came out of the sweep. Kaiser KS202 (mapper 56) had a read path to its `$6000` work RAM and no write path. Kaiser KS7032 (mapper 142) is modelled differently from its wiki page; that one is recorded and left open.

A register read that drives only some data bits now leaves the rest floating, through a new additive `Mapper::cpu_read_driven_mask`. Sachen 150/243's 3-bit registers and TCA-01's 6-bit protection read use it.

## Five boards get the RAM their wiki pages document

To see what the open-bus change did to real games, the local commercial-ROM suite was run on v2.7.1 and on this branch, and the results were compared snapshot by snapshot (its committed snapshots have drifted since June). Where a game read an empty window, open bus is the hardware answer. But five boards' wiki pages document RAM at `$6000` that the model never had: mappers 156, 177, 241 and 245, and mapper 227's battery-backed FW-01 variant. Writes to it had always vanished. They now have their 8 KiB, and the battery-backed ones save it.

With the suite's own input script, three games render differently from v2.7.1, all for the better:

| Game | v2.7.1 at frame 1100 | v2.7.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *Super Mario Bros. 3* (KS202 pirate, mapper 56) | a black screen | the World 1 map |
| *Buzz & Waldog* (two dumps, mapper 156) | a stats screen reading "POWER NONE" | World 1, Stage 1 |

Every other difference is in audio or cycle counts only, from games that read an empty `$6000` window.

## Ten boards accept a header correction

The per-game database may correct a header's mirroring bit only on a board whose mirroring is fixed in hardware. Mappers 11, 13, 34, 38, 79, 87, 94, 180 and 184, and 70 unless its header says four-screen, now say so, each checked against its wiki page. The audit also listed 71 and 152, but both control their own mirroring and stay excluded.

## Save states

The MMC1, MMC5 and Namco 163 blobs, and those of the five boards that gained RAM, each gain a trailing block. A save state from an earlier release still loads, and replays the way it was recorded.

## What this does not fix

**Kaiser KS7032 (mapper 142) is left open (F-09).** Its wiki page gives `$6000-$7FFF` an 8 KiB switchable PRG-ROM bank selected by register 4. The model reads a zeroed work RAM there until register 4 bit 2 selects ROM. That is a modelling divergence, not open bus, and it waits for a release that can check it against a game. The open-bus test names it in an allow-list, so it cannot pass silently.

Also out of scope, as planned:

- SZROM, which uses a CHR line for 16 KiB of PRG-RAM.
- MMC5's 128 KiB single-SRAM wiring, which the wiki describes as theoretical.
- Namco 163's `$F800` write-protect nibble.

The commercial-ROM comparison ran only locally, against dumps that are never committed, and with one input script. "0 regressed" covers the frames it rendered, not every game's full playthrough.

**Next:** v2.7.3 is the desktop and web release, and carries the desktop battery-save gap found in v2.7.1 (FE-01).
